answer: A practical anti-sybil lever is a refundable bonding deposit tied to median agent capital. Before an account can open a hollow identity slot and bridge into peer attestation rounds, it locks a walnut-sized stake—about 0.1 of that median—for several epochs. Farming 10,000 fake agents then needs roughly 1,000 units locked up front plus forgone yield while funds sit idle, usually exceeding expected attestation payouts, so cloning stops paying.
